text: Lesson 7 was explicit: TDE protects storage and backups, not a query an authorized account is allowed to run. Overlook has columns — a patient's date of birth, a phone number — where staff need to work with the row but don't need to see every sensitive value in plaintext.

Azure SQL offers two real options here: Dynamic Data Masking, which masks the query result in real time at low cost, and Always Encrypted, which encrypts the data client-side behind a key only a specific application holds. Overlook's real need is reporting and front-desk staff seeing most data normally with a few fields hidden from casual view — that's Dynamic Data Masking's job, not Always Encrypted's.

Applying it is a column-level ALTER TABLE statement: default masks a date of birth with a fixed placeholder, partial shows some real characters on a phone number while masking the middle, and email keeps an address's shape readable while hiding the account name. Only an account explicitly granted the UNMASK permission — Overlook's actual reporting account, not every front-desk login — ever sees the real values.

Masking reduces casual exposure, but it isn't a security boundary against a determined, permitted user, and it doesn't answer who actually accessed a record and when. That's next lesson: setting up real auditing.
